images.filename: Hillside down to Bardsey village - geograph.org.uk - 785466.jpg
images.caption: Hillside down to Bardsey village As you round the corner on the path down from the high point of Mynydd Enlli, the houses come into sight below. Beyond is the Irish Sea.
images.alt: Hillside down to Bardsey village As you round the corner on the path down from the high point of Mynydd Enlli, the houses come into sight below. Beyond is the Irish Sea.

images.caption: Approaching Cafn Enlli The narrow channel in the centre, with a yellow boat 'parked' above it, leads to the Bardsey slipway where everybody visiting the island disembarks.
images.alt: Approaching Cafn Enlli The narrow channel in the centre, with a yellow boat 'parked' above it, leads to the Bardsey slipway where everybody visiting the island disembarks.
categories: Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland

images.caption: Bardsey gate posts These gate posts, on an opening from the main track to a field, are extraordinarily large. They are also different - one is square and the other is round. There is no sign that a gate has ever been hung from them.  The boat house is visible left of centre.
images.alt: Bardsey gate posts These gate posts, on an opening from the main track to a field, are extraordinarily large. They are also different - one is square and the other is round. There is no sign that a gate has ever been hung from them.  The boat house is visible left of centre.
categories: Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland

images.filename: Engineering relics near the lighthouse - geograph.org.uk - 903251.jpg
images.caption: Engineering relics near the lighthouse These artefacts, on the west coast, look a bit like a wartime gun emplacement, but are perhaps more likely to be linked with the lighthouse construction as the light tower is only 50 metres away.
images.alt: Engineering relics near the lighthouse These artefacts, on the west coast, look a bit like a wartime gun emplacement, but are perhaps more likely to be linked with the lighthouse construction as the light tower is only 50 metres away.
categories: Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland

images.filename: From one side to the other - geograph.org.uk - 903208.jpg
images.caption: From one side to the other At this point Bardsey Island is almost divided into two, being only about 40 metres wide. There is storm erosion visible on both sides, so potentially it will become two separate islands before long.
images.alt: From one side to the other At this point Bardsey Island is almost divided into two, being only about 40 metres wide. There is storm erosion visible on both sides, so potentially it will become two separate islands before long.
categories: Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland

images.filename: Heading back to the slipway from the lighthouse - geograph.org.uk - 903200.jpg
images.caption: Heading back to the slipway from the lighthouse Mynydd Enlli is in the distance. The yellow object in the centre of the photo is a boat parked at the top of the slipway.
images.alt: Heading back to the slipway from the lighthouse Mynydd Enlli is in the distance. The yellow object in the centre of the photo is a boat parked at the top of the slipway.

images.filename: Henllwyn, from the north west - geograph.org.uk - 903186.jpg
images.caption: Henllwyn, from the north west Henllwyn [Old Grove] is the far bay, with the boats. The inlet in front of the anchored boats leads to the Bardsey slipway. The boathouse is just visible centre right.
images.alt: Henllwyn, from the north west Henllwyn [Old Grove] is the far bay, with the boats. The inlet in front of the anchored boats leads to the Bardsey slipway. The boathouse is just visible centre right.
categories: Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland

images.caption: Henllwyn shore, with seals These rocks separate Henllwyn from Cafn Enlli, where the slipway is. The yellow boat is parked at the top of the slipway and there are three seals in the water right of centre.
images.alt: Henllwyn shore, with seals These rocks separate Henllwyn from Cafn Enlli, where the slipway is. The yellow boat is parked at the top of the slipway and there are three seals in the water right of centre.

images.filename: Looking south down the island - geograph.org.uk - 904603.jpg
images.caption: Looking south down the island Plas Bach house is on the left. The photo shows the fertile, though exposed, nature of the land in the south of the island.
images.alt: Looking south down the island Plas Bach house is on the left. The photo shows the fertile, though exposed, nature of the land in the south of the island.

images.filename: Looking towards the slipway wall, from Henllwyn - geograph.org.uk - 903240.jpg
images.caption: Looking towards the slipway wall, from Henllwyn The wall is the protective barrier, which also acts as a jetty when the tide is high enough and boats can moor in Cafn Enlli.
images.alt: Looking towards the slipway wall, from Henllwyn The wall is the protective barrier, which also acts as a jetty when the tide is high enough and boats can moor in Cafn Enlli.

images.caption:
Blaenau Ffestiniog railway station - On the left of the picture, Arriva Trains Wales British Rail Class 153 DMU 153327 stands at the standard gauge platform for a Conwy Valley Line service. While on the right of the picture the narrow gauge Ffestiniog Railway locomotive Linda is about to run-round the train in preparation for the journey to Porthmadog.

Note also the different platform heights for the different gauges.
